title: Bait and Switch
body: To begin with, the app is good. It strikes a balance between simplicity and quality of the features. If you never used it before and the idea of paying $50 a year for your entire life (or until the app is discontinued) doesn’t sound too bad of a deal, I would recommend to give it a try. So why 1 star? Up until last few days the app was free and the majority of the features that are now marked as Pro were included already. Just 6 months ago the developer was advertising the app on Reddit with claims like “It’s 100% free - no subscriptions, purchase, limits”. And now when people got their recipes in, the model is switched and there is no way out. If you don’t need to import more than 1 recipe a week you can still have access to your collection for free, but it is now turned into a glorified notes storage. Ironically you can’t even add notes as you cook with it to your own recipes (only Pro has this feature now). So how is it different from keeping your recipes in note taking app with basic tagging support, or in a PDF collection? I don’t think business practices like this should be rewarded. Building reputation and then adding paid tier for new optional features makes total sense, but getting customer’s data and commitment first and then making the app useless without subscription does not.

title: Amazing ingredients shopping app, okay cooking app
body: I primarily use crouton as my recipe manager app, and deglaze I think has earned a spot in addition to it, but not replacing it. Whats to like: The single biggest draw for me is how the app handles grocery lists. It breaks it down by food category and by recipe. The autoscaling is also great. I love the fact that if I change my mind about which recipe I’m going to cook that week it removes those ingredients from the shopping list. Simply put that is amazing and this alone is worth keeping the app. Mixed reviews: Recipe importer, for some things its amazing. It picked up a recipe in a reddit post with amazing ease (something paprika and crouton failed at). However giving it some serious eat recipes makes it absolute choke and take forever (which is kind of funny given how those are actually properly formatted) Recipe management, tags work okay, it would be nice if auto suggested some or let you batch tag things better. Cooking instructions: When you use the app to “cook along” (not sure the term but to follow a recipe instructions in app) its generally a good experience. Unlike other apps it keeps all the instructions up at once instead of breaking down each step into a unique card or whatever and highlights it. Sometimes this is a mixed bag, but generally I think I like it. Recipe Timers: The timers are pretty intuitive the only issue being some of the recipes with a range (ie let sit for 10-20 minutes) it always seems to grab the low end. You can add time in the timers view. Since they are in the app and not through Siri you can’t voice control them, which is actually kind of a pain. That is one my main uses of Siri and other assistants is to control cooking timers hands free since frequently when the alarm is going off your hands are occupied. What could be better: Website following seems oddly limited. Several sites I use have their own RSS feeds and other managers like crouton see it on recipe import and ask if I would like to follow it. Deglaze only lets you follow “pre-approved” sites/people. You can submit a request to have something added, but that seems entirely unnecessary and I wish it would prompt on recipe import like others. Lack of MacOS/web support. I do most of my recipe browsing on MacOS (then use iOS for shopping, and iPadOS when cooking), so the lack of support for desktop is annoying. If they enabled the iPad app to run on M-series Macs that would also be fine. Currently I use iPhone mirroring and it sort of works but isn’t ideal. Calendar meal planner: I don’t know why, but I use this feature so much in other apps, but it’s how I layout my week so its absence is keenly felt here.

title: The best recipe app by far
body: I never leave reviews but just had to because I love this app so much. I trialed a ton of recipe apps about a year ago and this was the best by far for my needs. I still use it near daily a year later. The importing works really well even with screenshots or poorly taken photos. The in-recipe timers are a godsend for multi-part recipes. The automatic recalculation for scaling a recipe not just in the ingredients list but inline in the instructions is great. The household joint account feature is SO handy; my partner and I save recipes as we find them and then pick a few for the week and add them to the shopping list (and the shopping list sorting by aisle and by recipe is such a great feature too!). I’ve also found a ton of my favorite recipes just browsing the explore section. I have ADHD so the coordination of cooking can be struggle for me, but I’ve built my cooking repertoire so much thanks to Deglaze and I really love cooking with it. I’m a big cheapskate and never pay for apps or subscriptions, but paying for this is such a no brainer for me.

body: This app is the answer to all of your modern-day cooking problems! With this app, you no longer share it with your favorites. Instead, you share it with the Deglaze app. Then, you opened the app, and it is saved in your “library” of recipes. you open your library and a list of the titles of the recipe and pictures are shown, you simply choose the recipe you just saved, and it will give you all the ingredients where you can check them off at the store then it gives you the instructions how to make it and it’s all saved, conveniently right in this app. You can even change the portions that you wanna create so if you wanna serve two times that amount that it’s set to make you hit the two times button and all your ingredients will adjust. title: Amazing App, a few changes would make it perfect. So sad it’s no longer free.
body: Absolutely love this app, by far the BEST app out there for recipe collecting and organization. So many useful features that other apps are missing (X-ray mode is my favorite), I love that there are no adds, the scale/convert feature is so useful, and I love how easy it is to import/upload recipes from photos, websites, etc. It’s amazing. 4 things that would make it better: - Really wish it was compatible with android phones so I could share recipes with more family/friends. This is my biggest request (my husband has an android and we both do a lot of cooking/baking, it’s hard having all the recipes on my phone only). - It would be really nice to have an online version that I could use on my computer. - Wish there was an easy way to print recipes from the app especially from X-ray mode. - Really wish it could stay free. I’ve been waiting for this to happen… and the day as come. They will now be charging for a subscription. I was really hoping this was just somebody’s passion project haha. If they had an option for donations rather than making people pay, I would totally donate now and then, but I don’t want to pay for a subscription, it’s just another thing to pay for and I don’t want to. If it was a little cheaper, or a reasonable one-time-fee rather than a subscription, and available to android users, I think I’d pay for it, but for now, I’m on my own again when it comes to recipe organization. So sad. They will have a free version of the app, but I don’t think it will be very useful compared to other apps. All my favorite features will be mostly unavailable without a subscription. However, if you’re willing to pay for a subscription, (unlike me), this app will make your life in the kitchen much easier.

title: Never review - but this deserves it
body: This is literally the first time I’m publicly reviewing an app because this 100% deserves to be shared. It is a fantastic app. I have always been the person to save recipes on Instagram, in my notes app, in text threads. I finally fell for the Instagram adds advertising other recipe consolidation apps but all the ones I tried were more of a hassle than my old method. I saw this suggested on Reddit and tried it. I have never seen an app more carefully and considerately programed. I genuinely don’t know which feature is my favorite but it’s so intuitive and not overwhelming at all. All the steps in the recipe are shown at once so you don’t have to go back and forth to see what’s coming up. You can click on each step in the recipe you are on to highlight it and not lose your place. You can click on timers directly in the recipe and run multiple timers at once. (It even tells you exactly how long PAST a timer something is if you are like me and like to cook some things a little extra). I honestly didn’t think I could like a utility app so much but this was so clearly carefully and thoughtfully designed and developed, and for FREE, they deserve recognition. I haven’t used the extra functions like sharing recipes with others or subscribing to find recipe suggestions - honestly it seems like goodreads but for recipes which is cool but not my reason for the app. It’s easy to ignore those features and just stick to my recipes.

This app is the crown jewel of all recipe apps. Simply a diamond in the rough. The fact it is free and doesn’t require a sub for any of the features that other apps charge for and don’t perform nearly half as good as this one is mind blowing. I follow a lot of cooking accounts on Instagram and bookmarking them into folders was getting tedious. This app letting you import a from a link with IG has worked perfectly. As long as they have the recipe laid out in the description it’s going to import it in a beautiful, clean and well laid out manner maintaining simplicity and modern layout. Will even tell you what app/site it was imported from and let you click to the video in app to IG with one click. The ability to add that recipe to a shopping list in a very simple and straight forward way has been a game changer. It just works and it’s very intuitive. You’re able to get in and out of the store in half the time and time is key so you can get on with your day. There is so many your features too. Measurement conversions, ability to covert the measurements to increase the serving size on the fly. Put your recipes in collections and categorize the recipes even with AI is incredible. As I mentioned, stupid simple and intuitive and sooooo much more. Feature rich while still keeping it simple and modern. Some quality of life suggestions I would like to see added. Ability to set a dark mode from the options. Certainly not a dealbreaker as the modern white layout is incredible as is and easy to read. I just prefer dark mode if available. Would love to see a “cook mode” option which would keep the screen on when following the recipe so you don’t always have to keep opening your phone or tablet. Your screen would always be on as long as the app is open. You need to get this app right now. You won’t be disappointed. You can import from social, websites, pictures, create your own from manual input you name it and it will lay it out in a simple intuitive beautiful way and make a shopping list from one click. Might add, will even let you uncheck items from the list that you might already have before you send it to the shopping list so you only get what you need. I’m extremely impressed with this app and has been just what I have been needing and looking for. Get it NOW! A++++++

body: This app is incredible for helping me manage cooking as a neurodivergent woman. It syncs seamlessly on my iPad AND my iPhone. You can search recipes, save them to your library, import them from socials/online blogs etc. You can also add all the ingredients from a recipe to a grocery list, with single tap. The sharing capabilities are seamless; my partner and I have shared for our meal planning, which also includes the grocery list. Our shopping trips are divide-and-conquer and twice as fast now, since we can see in real time what the other person is getting as they check the item off the list. The Live Cooking mode is incredible. It allows you to check off ingredients step by step as you add them, in addition to highlighting whichever your current step is. There’s great personalization in the app; I made the font super big on my iPad so I could see it across the kitchen while I was using a mixer, etc. There’s also a tab that lets you add notes to specific recipes, so that you can reference what you need later!! It will also scale recipes for you (double batch, half recipe, etc). This app is probably the GREATEST thing to happen to my cooking and meal planning journey, and I’m pretty sure I’m underutilizing many of its incredible features.

title: The most effortless cooking app
body: Cooking for health, deliciousness and variety has always meant that I have different recipes from different blogs and chefs that I have to either recall from memory or have to fight past pesky ads to get to the actual ingredient and recipe list. With Deglaze, it is so simple to just ‘pull and store’ the recipe in the app and be able to easily access the instructions while cooking. Love it and highly recommend it to anyone who likes to cook but not stress!

title: Awesome home cooking app!
body: Loving this app! From easy to create grocery lists to a flow of new and exciting recipes this app has everything a home cook could want. Whether you’re a seasoned home chef or just trying to cook a little more often, this app has every you need. Highly recommended a download to try it for yourself!

title: Deglaze is great!
body: I used to make a recipe I found on the internet by copying all the ingredients to a checklist and then scrolling up and down to see how much of what to add when. Later when I wanted to make that same recipe I’d have to sift through the hundred different individuals making the same recipe to find the one I liked. With Deglaze I import the recipe once and everything is done for you. It lets you add all of the ingredients to a shared shopping list with your family, flip seamlessly between ingredients and recipe instructions and even supports timers. All of my recipes are stored in Deglaze and you can even search your recipes by ingredient when you find you have too much eggplant and no idea what to do with it. I also find the feed of what others have cooked to be inspiring. I have found many great recipes from the other users on Deglaze. Overall it’s a very helpful app for going from recipe to dinner!
